subject: Private footprint activation — tenant wiring, cross-subnet routing, and ops acceptance
messages:
From: Caroline Park <caroline.park@nimbushealth.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: engops@nimbushealth.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private footprint onboarding — initial wiring questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We need a concise checklist from Redwood that we can share with our networking and security teams so they can prepare the VPC/physical rack wiring, firewall rules, and peering topology for the private footprint (on-prem edge). Goal is to have Day 0-ready environment by July 8.

Top concerns from our side:
- Confirm required NAT, public VIPs, and whether floating IPs are needed for the control-plane components.
- Egress allowlist: we'll need a minimal set of outbound domains/IPs for telemetry, model pull, and S3 access.
- Port/ACLs between admin bastion, inference nodes, and KMS/HSM network.
- Any recommended MTU/peering settings for cross-subnet KV cache replication.

I've attached our baseline network diagram and a proposed timeline. Can you send a short punchlist we can attach to our internal MOP?

Cheers,
Caroline
Caroline Park
Head of Infrastructure, Nimbus Health

Attachments: nimbus-network-diagram-v2.png (image/png), timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Caroline Park <caroline.park@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private footprint onboarding — initial wiring questions

Caroline —

Thanks for the clear list. I've sketched a focused Day0 checklist below and attached a short mutual-action-plan (MAP) PDF. I copied Ben and Karthik for the infra/ops and networking runbook items. This checklist assumes: we will deploy a control-plane in your isolated management subnet, inference pools in tenant subnets, and a dedicated egress gateway for telemetry.

Minimum Day 0 checklist (deliverable items) — please confirm these with your network team:
1) IP addressing: provide /22 for tenant inference subnets and /28 for control-plane VIPs. Confirm if you prefer RFC1918 ranges or routed public blocks for inbound admin flow.
2) NAT/Egress: reserve a single NAT gateway IP that will be used for outbound telemetry and S3/model pulls; provide allowlist exceptions (see attached egres-allowlist sample).
3) Routing: create static routes from tenant subnets to the egress gateway; ensure BGP sessions to edge router if you're using dynamic routing.
4) Firewall rules (suggested):
   - Control-plane (TCP 443, 22023) from Redwood bastion only
   - Inference nodes: outbound TCP 443 to S3 and telemetry endpoints; inbound inter-node TCP range 10000-11000 for KV/cache replication (or UDP if policy requires)
   - KMS/HSM: allow only from control-plane management subnet, restrict to required ports per vendor
5) MTU: prefer 9000 if your fabric supports jumbo frames for faster model shard transfers; otherwise 1500 default.
6) DNS: provide an internal DNS zone for control-plane discovery entries; we will publish service names on deployment.
7) Certificates/Trust: we will consume your CA bundle; provide an API for cert rotation or confirm use of in-cloud KMS.
8) Monitoring hooks: open port for outbound telemetry (TCP 443) to telemetry.redwood.ai and provide any internal proxy details.
9) Ops access: identify 2 day-0 oncall engineers and provide SSH key fingerprints for the bastion.

I attached the MAP and an example egress-allowlist CSV. Ben — can you confirm the KV port range and whether we should prefer TCP or UDP for intra-pod replication in Nimbus' environment?

Next steps: Caroline to confirm IP plan and egress IP by Monday 2027-06-28. We'll follow with a Day0 smoke test plan and a short preflight runbook.

- Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: nimbus-mutual-action-plan.pdf (application/pdf), egress-allowlist-sample.csv (text/csv)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, Caroline Park <caroline.park@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private footprint onboarding — initial wiring questions

Caroline, Priyom — quick notes from infra/serving runtime perspective:

- KV cache replication: we recommend TCP 10080-10085 (TCP) for control traffic and 11000-11010 for bulk shard transfer. TCP gives more predictable behavior across enterprise firewalls; we'll fall back to UDP only if you have strict constraints.
- Ports for model-pull: outbound 443 to S3 endpoints and registry.redwood.ai for image/model manifests.
- Bastion flow: prefer a forwarded SSH with port 22023 mapped to internal control-plane API; keep 22 closed to the internet.
- Healthcheck endpoints: allow HTTP/HTTPS probes from our control-plane IPs for deployment smoke tests (we'll provide exact IPs in the MAP).

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Deployment Orchestration, Redwood Inference
From: Caroline Park <caroline.park@nimbushealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private footprint onboarding — initial wiring questions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our network team after internal review:
- We'll expose the control-plane VIPs on RFC1918 (10.42.0.0/28) and keep tenant subnets in 10.43.0.0/22.
- NAT will be a single egress IP; we'll provide the address by EOD Monday.
- MTU: we can enable jumbo frames (9000) across the fabric; we'll confirm with our colo provider about cross-rack consistency.
- KMS: we are using an on-prem HSM; we will allow access from the control-plane subnet over the vendor-prescribed port 15002.

We'll attach Ben's port list to our MOP and share the egress IP + SSH key fingerprints Monday. Also scheduling a 30-minute joint preflight call on Tuesday 2027-06-29 at 10:00 PT to walk through the smoke tests.

-Caroline
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Caroline Park <caroline.park@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private footprint onboarding — initial wiring questions

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Caroline. That plan looks good. For the Tuesday preflight we'll bring a short checklist and the Day0 smoke script (connectivity, model pull, KV replication sanity, KMS handshake). Please add the JIRA ticket RED-9273 to any notes so we can sync post-call.

Deliverables before the call:
- Nimbus: provide egress IP, bastion SSH key fingerprints, and confirmation of MTU across racks.
- Redwood: provide final MAP with exact healthcheck IPs and Day0 smoke script.

We'll aim to execute Day0 on July 8 as discussed, assuming the preflight passes.

Thanks — talk Tuesday.
Priyom
